content: Mortis A time for love, a time for hate, a time for peace ,  and a time for war. - Book of Aurtus "It is not like him to make someone of your stature wait, Lord Speaker," the older woman stated gracefully making her way across the large marble study.  The staccato sound of her wooden shoes echoing off the cavernous stone walls caused Darius to wince at each hit of the oak heel against the virgin white stone.  The older woman caught the reaction, a small smile adorning her face as she came to stand before him. Despite her advanced age, her movements were sure and steady as if that of someone much younger, he thought.  Darius stood stalwart the only movement was his eyes, tracking the woman with feigned disinterest, with a smile, she moved again, disappearing beyond even his peripheral vision.  Darius quickly felt the heat of her stare on the back of his neck, the feeling uncomfortable, and Darius turned to face her, realizing too late she had forced him to move.  She has bested me , he thought wincing internally,  so it was to be power games  he surmised. This woman was taking his measure; he regarded her coolly,  studying her every detail .  The woman's steel grey demeanor lent to her disposition as well as her coloring; thirty years previous, she would have been able to easily get by with her looks  he realized, but to be in the Kings inner circle at her age, she was someone to be reckoned with .  Darius met her  eyes,  taking in the harsh but pleasant features of her face .   She continued to observe him quietly, Darius suppressing a shiver; as their eyes locked, he could see a predatory  gaze  in her stare, like looking into the dead, black eyes of a shark he mused. This Woman was calculating and deliberate, every movement, motion, and position purposely thought out, like a game of chess, eliciting reactions, assessing them, looking for weaknesses.  Darius knew this game well and knew how to play; this was a woman of the court, a woman whose job was to understand him; she was the King's advanced team. The Speaker was no stranger to the games of royalty; in his time as a Speaker, he had come head to head with Princes and Kings.  This Woman would not best him, he affirmed, Darius turned to face the Woman, keeping his back straight and shoulders squared, giving the impression of strength.  Despite feeling like he had none, he refused to show fear or confusion, instead keeping his face neutral, despite being taken by force from his sanctuary.  Quietly he continued to track the Woman as she half turned gracefully, gliding across the room to the old mahogany standing bar in the corner of the study.  With expert movements, she plucked a glass deftly from under the standing bar and began pouring something dark into a crystal snifter. The Woman motioned with the bottle towards Darius and waited a moment, with a shake of his head, he refused the proffered drink.  The Woman shrugged, a small smile spreading over her face as she finished pouring and then, in one swift motion, brought the tumbler to her lips and downed the amber liquid in a single gulp. The old woman slightly bowed to the Lord Speaker,  and I pass another test , Darius thought, returning the bow, both showing respect to the other. Darius lowered his cowl, finally revealing his striking features, the old woman getting her first real look at the Lord Speaker.  He took in the reaction to his bright blue eyes as they stood out against his dark Mediterranean skin and black hair.  He noticed the slight widening of the woman's eyes, not uncommon, he thought.  The Speaker knew his features were a rarity in this region, a gift from his long-deceased mother.  She had been an eastern immigrant, a stranger to this land when she had met his father, a woman whose swarthy looks were ordinary in her home country, but rare and very noticeable here, in a land of alabaster skin and blonde hair. Darius took a calming breath, getting control of the anger and impatience that had shadowed his mood since being whisked away to this place.  He had remained alone in this study for the entire day.  Darius had fallen back on his training, so here he had stood, motionless for the last eight hours, focusing only on every detail of this room. Using the time to take in every clue available to him within the place.  Since entering the study under escort from the royal guard that morning, he had collected quite a bit of information.  The Speaker knew the simple meditative state was unsettling for others to see; they would quickly grow uncomfortable.  They had always felt the need to fill the silent space with   movement and sound.  This had been an advantage during the questioning of subjects as a Speaker.  Darius smiled  as he recalled  how well it had worked over the years,  a benefit of his training,   one of the first lessons learned as a child when upon the path of Speaker.   The Speaker studied the woman's expensive blue silk gown and handmade alabaster shoes. She  is a woman of means, someone who has had to adapt within a court of men.  To hold a position of power like this, she had to be better by far than any man . He thought his eyes coming to settle on the deep lines of her face.  Her face spoke of skill and competence, her advanced age told of shrewd experience,  her easygoing smile and the relaxed manner is a mask  he thought.  Again,  he returned to her eyes ,  her  calculating eyes held something else, something almost feral, he mused, vowing not to underestimate this wolf in grandma's clothing and then suppressed a smirk at the analogy. "It is fine. I am sure the King has much to do," Darius responded, speaking for the first time his pleasant, almost melodic voice lending to sell his forced pleasantry, Darius would keep his ego in check.  He would not allow the actions of this impertinent King to dictate his response, the King had overstepped his authority, but he didn't need to point that out, didn't need to yell and threaten.  No, this man would not have done such a thing without reason,  understand, empathize, visualize the motive  he thought again relying on the teaching of the priests. "Do you know why I was summoned this day?" he asked the woman, his tone still easy as he tried to pry what information Darius could from her, observing he caught the moment the woman registered the question.  Her body language quickly changing, becoming stiff as she merely shook her head, the smile faltering for only a moment,  she knows  he thought,  she knows and was ordered to be silent .   Darius had been removed by soldiers from the keep, from his very sanctuary, anger flashing through his mind at the thought, those actions  alone  would be enough to anger the  Church  elders, or worse, his mind continued.  This King threatened the peace that had cost so much innocent blood only two generations previous.  To break that peace would mean a world bathed in blood, Darius remembering the history lessons of the Blood King's reign and the Mage Wars,  he  shivered  recalling  reading of the bloody battles and slaughter and torture of innocents, all in the name of  purity. A  Speaker's position was beyond the authority of this world.  No one dared to interfere with a speaker performing the duties of his office. He answered to no man, no mortal law, and certainly no King. His eyes shifted away from the old woman to the rows and rows of books along the walls. The collection was well used, so if this was indeed the King's study, then the man was incredibly well-read, he thought. The woman was quiet for only a moment and then spoke with carefully measured words. "Speaker Darius, your escort here was not decided lightly, and the King is well aware he tempts fate with his actions, but I assure you once you hear what he has to say, you will understand. I will tell you this is probably the most important case you have ever taken" she finished her eyes watching for any reaction, Darius gave none. The two stood there staring at each other, neither speaking a word, the quiet quickly grew uncomfortable.  A voice broke the silence, startling them out of their thoughts, turning in unison to view the new arrival. "I apologize for keeping you waiting," came the friendly voice from the door.  Darius  caught the woman’s penitent action out of the corner of his eye .  King Alaric , he thought,  taking in the tall grey-haired figure as he stepped into the room .   A  forced smile playing across the tall man's features as he made a dismissive motion for the woman to stand, turning his attention to Darius at once.  The smile never  leaving his face , he waited for only a moment for  The Speaker  to bow as well, Darius did not .  The King moved on, making no mention nor showing any displeasure at the man's spurn. The woman eyed Darius, and out of his peripheral vision, he could make out the disapproval playing across her face.  He was usually not this stubborn but damn it to Artus. He had been kidnapped and kept waiting.  Darius tracked the woman as she quietly made her way to the door and paused by the King, the two exchanging a meaningful glance and a few soft words.  The King nodding as she stepped, passed him, and disappeared out of the room. King Alaric stepped quickly towards the center of the study to the gathering of sparse furniture. With a practiced theatrical flourish, he swept the long green silk gown out of the way and settled into a large brown leather chair facing Darius.  The smile still on the man's face,  the eyes  he thought  were holding back a tsunami of emotion the King was doing his best to hide . Darius observed as he quietly took the other man in.  He allowed his eyes to take in every detail of Alaric, seeing the tired features of his eyes and the nervous movement of his hands  Interesting  Darius thought, adding that to the arsenal of information he had already collected that day. Without even a by your leave, Darius took control of the moment. Taking a step forward, he began to speak with purpose,  "Your Majesty, you flaunt authority you do not have with your actions, please tell me you do not tempt the breaking of the peace that has lasted so long simply because your son was killed.  I understand this will shake your rule as it leaves ascension to the throne uncertain but listening to an advisor who would tell you to kidnap a Speaker, despite your reservations, is near madness" Darius shot at the man, allowing the annoyance of the day to enter his voice. The man's smile never left his face; however, his head shifted slightly to the side, the curious look almost comical Darius thought as the King nodded.  "She has told you much, I am surprised, but your right, it was her idea and a daring one at that," he said, Darius waving off the comment continuing to pace the study. "Rest easy, King, she did not divulge anything, I am a Speaker, this is what we do." Darius began and then pointed to the shelves. "The library is vast, the layer of dust near the lip of the shelves is evident, except for in front of one book, the book of succession.  Which means someone has been looking into who succeeds the throne should you or your son die," Darius continued pacing as he gave voice to his thoughts, his tone that of an instructor to an impertinent student. "The vials on the table smell of almonds, which means its Cyanide, however, the vials were moved aside, and the slight indentations in the table show that someone has been copying runic script. From that, I can conclude your son was not poisoned but allegedly killed with magic," he continued. Observing the King as his eyes narrowed, shifting away from the Speaker to study the tabletop trying to see what the Speaker had.  Darius knew the King would not see the slight indentations a quill made in soft pine. It took years of training and a command of magic to see it, Darius brought his lesson to a conclusion, "And finally I caught the look between the two of you and heard her whisper give him a chance, making the entire scenario obvious.  The Speaker did not sit, would not yield to this sovereign, proving the King was not the power in this room. For Darius was a servant of the keep, he answered to one who was greater than even Alaric.  The King studied Darius, the smile falling from his face as grief overtook the man causing the Speaker to pause.  This was more than simple politics for Alaric. He truly grieved for the death of his son. A King was not an everyman; he had seen more than one powerful man worry more about the effects than the actual death of a close relative.  Darius realized he should have noticed that the fact he hadn't made him reflect upon his jaded nature and wince internally.  He came to sit across from this grieving father, settling into an identical leather chair.  Shifting in the chair, Darius appreciated the well-worn leather and soft stuffing of the well-crafted furniture; these were not here for decoration. He indeed was in the King's inner sanctum, which spoke volumes about this meeting. Reaching over and laying a gentle hand on the King's arm, the action did not go unnoticed as the King nodded in thanks. "I know what I have done is a crime, hell what I have done could undo the damned Agreement, but Lord Speaker, I don't care, I need to know who killed Banis. He was my world and has been since my wife was taken from me; someone is playing a cruel game.  Speaker, and I beg you to find out who," he began. Pausing as he collected himself and Darius could see the pain in this man's posture, radiating out from him in waves.  Alaric gathered himself, his watery eyes holding back a deluge of tears as his voice shook, with an effort of will, he continued to speak, "My son is dead, the light of my life, and he has been taken from me," the King began as his facelifted.  Despite the thick black beard, Darius could see his jaw set forward as the deluge finally broke free, streaming down his face, the torchlight reflecting against the river of sorrow along his face. Darius watched the man as he emotionally unraveled. Yes, this man had threatened to break the Agreement, the compact between Church, Mage, and Mundane, the pact that allowed all three to live in peace.  Darius reflected as his hand went unconsciously to the brand on his cheek, that one that marked him as a Mage, one of the concessions made to stop the killing of his people when the Agreement was signed. Alaric's voice grew hard the pain and grieving, transforming to anger as his face grew cold and his eyes distant, breaking Darius from his thoughts as the King spoke.  "He was killed to ensure I had no heir, I know it, there are those who wish to end my reign, to end the line of my family ruling this land, they mean to exterminate my bloodline Speaker, this cannot, this will not happen," the King declared. Darius settled back into the chair, this was not the first time he had listened to a parent recall the death of their child, and though it was something he had done many times, he felt the man's pain.  Could see how it was eating him alive, as if a hole had suddenly appeared in his soul, eroding the substance that made him corporeal.  If Alaric did not gain control of himself, hide this weakness, this pain, his court would descend upon him like a pack of hungry wolves, devouring the man even if he wasn't outright killed.  The court would find a way to take control, Alaric could find himself a puppet King; the Speaker studied this man, this father, this King.  The logical tactician gave way to the man, no the priest he realized with surprise, his heart went out to Alaric, not the King, but for this grieving father; on the outside, Darius remained stoic, allowing the King to take his time and tell the story.  Alaric looked as if he had aged ten years in an instant as he recalled the grizzly scene of his sons' demise. "The servants found him yesterday, in his room, slumped over his table. The look on his face…, th-the blood, it is as if he vomited every ounce within him" The King paused.  Gathering his will, the picture of his son, dead burned into his brain, he began to recall every detail. "The look on his face was one of pain Speaker; someone had caused him so much pain, his muscles were twisted as if he were trying to claw off his skin."  As the last words echoed off the stone study, the only sound heard was the King's soft sobbing. After a time, Darius leaned forward, "I will Speak for your son, my King," he whispered, watching as the other man's shoulders slumped with relief. With those words, Darius had absolved the King of his crime against himself and the Church.  By taking on this task, he had given his bond, his word that Darius, Speaker of Aurtus, would now tell the story of this man's son.  He would search out those responsible and bring their dark deed into the light; no man could stand in his way; no place was forbidden, for he was the bringer of truth and light. Nothing stood in the way of a Speaker once his bond was given. He would bring this grieving father the truth of his son's brutal death, no matter to where or to whom it led. A few moments later, Darius found himself being led by an old man dressed in well-polished light leather armor. A  retired soldier, given the honor of house guard , he thought, looking the man over.  The Soldier was hobbling forward an injury on his right leg, causing a very pronounced limp. Darius observed he tried to keep track of the route they were taking but failed miserably.  Having spent the day in the large warm study, Darius became keenly aware of the sun going down.  The cold October evening was settling into the old stone castle.  Pulling the thin grey robe around him, he did his best to battle the chilly air as he was led through hall after hall, around corners and down long flights of stairs. "The body is kept in the lower level to keep it cool," the gravelly voice of the old Soldier announced as the two made their way down the third flight of stairs. Descending once again for what seemed like an eternity, the torch carried by the old man quickly became the only light.  The waxing moon coming in through windows now fading as they descended into the dark earth. Darius could see the change in the stone as they fell beneath the ground, the old stone becoming damp and moss-covered.  The further they descended, the more treacherous the footing became. Darius felt his leather sandals giving way to the slick rock beneath his feet.  The Speaker marveled at the surety of the elderly man, descending at a good clip despite the limp and never losing his footing. The men entered a narrow hall, the damp walls.   Darius reached out and carefully touched the dripping water as it lovingly caressed a newly formed stalactite. This section of the castle was slowly being taken back by the subterranean plants he noticed as Darius eyed the lush vines flourishing from cracks in the stone walls and flowing over the damp mossed ridden floor. Finally, the Soldier stopped, pointing to a large wooden door. "I will go no further, Lord Speaker, but what you seek is within that room," he stated, Darius looking at him curiously and seeing fear in this man's eyes, the torchlight casting an eerie light on his thin white hair and dark brown eyes. The old man offered no other words, merely stood there patiently waiting for Darius to continue, as Darius turned towards the dark entrance. He caught the motion as the Soldier made a quick furtive motion with his hand. It was old Darius recalled trying to remember the name of the ancient, pagan religion and then smiled, Catholicism. The man had made a cross in the air, and as he walked towards the light at the end of the hall, Darius heard the man begin a soft chant in an ancient language "Hail Mary, full of grace…"  People still practiced that dark religion  he mused moving away from the Soldier. Reaching the large decaying wooden door, Darius grasped the handle when, suddenly, to his surprise, it swung open, revealing a squat, fat man with a contagious grin and bright, intelligent eyes. "Hello, Lord Speaker," the rotund man began excitedly, his bald head covered in sweat despite the chill in the air "it is quite the honor to meet one such as you, please, please  come in," the man said excitedly, taking a small cloth to his shiny dome, moving to the side to allow Darius to enter. The Speaker cautiously entered the small room, wincing at the stench of decay that hung heavy in the air. It was apparent the Prince had been dead a while before he had been brought here to speak, pushing out with his will Darius whispered "non nidore," his blue eyes flashing white as he infused the words with his will. The smell immediately dissipated. Sometimes  it's good to be a  Mage , The Speaker mused, feeling the small man's gaze light upon him. Darius turned his head and regarded the man coolly; he knew the man was staring at the deep red dragon brand on his cheek, the mark that identified him as a  Mage . "You are a  Mage ," the little bald man said, though it sounded more a question than a statement, Darius nodded. "Yet you are of the  Church , despite what the priests of Aurtus have done to your people," he finished again. The statement was more of a question. Darius shook his head; it had not been the first time someone had stared unbelievingly at the Mage, who served under men whose ancestors had more than once tried to exterminate his people. The Agreement had changed all of that, Iseni, so strong and sure had led her people to a stalemate with  the King dom  and the  Church , forcing them to capitulate and allowed Mages to become full citizens for the first time in ages. Darius was quiet a moment and then nodded at the man. "I am a  Mage , but more importantly, I am a Speaker, I serve Aurtus, not the priests or the King; however, to be a Speaker, one must have the power to manipulate their surroundings, one must be a  Mage  and a priest." He finished. The man stood there confused, his eyes staring into nowhere as he processed Darius's words. Finally, his gaze returned to Darius, and he nodded with a smile. "Alright, your holy spellcaster, let's see what the young prince can tell us; they wouldn't let me examine the body until you had arrived," the little man stated excitedly, smiling at his joke, turning away, he stopped. Darius could see him wince and turn back, "I apologize, Lord Speaker, I am Murat, I am the one who takes care of those passed," Murat said, motioning to the Lord Speaker to follow as he made his way towards the center of the small room and to the table. "Murat, are you a doctor by chance?" Darius asked, not daring to hope, a doctor could be invaluable this evening in helping to identify what had happened to this man, but his hopes were quickly dashed as Murat shook his head "more like an undertaker, my Lord. I take the bodies and ensure that the relatives can stomach to look at them, then I display them for the proper 12 days so that everyone can say goodbye to the deceased," he finished as his voice trailed off, Murat's eyes followed the sheet edges. He did not move to remove the cloth, and Darius did not blame him; this death was not pleasant. With a slight nod, Darius turned to focus on what lay upon the old butcher's table, the worn table where the body lay looked to have been used to butcher pigs before its new life as an examining table, he thought. His eyes playing along the angular gashes in the edge of the worn wood, they told a tale of suffering as his mind calculated the strength and angle of each indentation, pulling himself away from the simple exercise, he focused on what lay upon the table. His eyes followed the contours of the simple white sheet, his mind identifying legs and arms, the body was somehow twisted, wrong, he thought, trying to understand what he was seeing. He moved closer, coming to stand next to the table, looking down upon the covered body gave him no more clue to the oddness of the corpses angle. Murat waddled past Darius giving the Lord Speaker a slight bow as he made his way over to the body, gently, almost reverently he pulled the sheet off to reveal the grey bloated body of the young Prince. Despite the yellowing corpse being well past rigor, his face still held the ghastly scream that had signaled the young man's demise; dried blood spread across the macabre scream lent to the King's tale of blood. "Who has been here to see the body?" Darius asked with detached professionalism when the man didn't answer. Darius looked up curiously, noticing the small man was transfixed by the Prince's death scream. He couldn't blame the man. Though he had probably seen just as many dead bodies as the Speaker himself, the look of fear and pain on the greying face was enough to make even the most hardened man pause. Snapping his fingers, he quickly got Murat's attention. "I'm sorry, Speaker," Murat stammered, "just, the pain he must have felt" Darius could hear the fear and empathy in the man's tone. Nodding in Agreement, he understood. "How many have come to view the body" Darius repeated; this time, the pause from Murat was cerebral as he thought over the past week finally, with a nod, "seven Speaker," he said, his tone sure. Not many, he thought, knowing at least three of them would have been the King, the old woman, and the head of security. The others were not that important. The killer most likely would not have scheduled time with the body, Darius thought, stepping closer and looking over the body. Circling the table, he studied the dead Prince allowing the details to wash over his mind, opening his perception, putting the training of the keep  to use , controlling his breathing no area of the young Prince went overlooked. "No signs of bruising or scratching, minimal signs of a struggle,  except for…" Darius began and trailed off, taking a closer look at the poor man's face. Studying the contours of the Prince's face, he could see the tightened jaw and creases from his furrowing brow. This man had seen death coming and knew what had killed him. He realized that whatever the cause of his demise, it was engineered to cause maximum pain for the victim. Darius continued to search the young dead princes' expression. After a few contemplative moments, he turned to Murat, "you might want to step back," he said, the undertaker giving him a curious look. Still, Murat took a few involuntary steps back towards the door, his eyes never leaving the table or Darius himself. Blowing out a breath, the Speakers eyes never leaving the body as he continued to collect clues. His hand begun to roll the sleeve up his left arm up, Murat's eyes went to the arm as ornate leather wraps were slowly revealed. Looking, Murat could see it started with a Jeweled leather band, thick with markings burned deep into its surface. Coming off of the bracelet were delicate leather tassels, intertwined and covering the entire forearm, each tassel carefully engraved with crystal runic script. Murat stepped closer, fear being replaced with curiosity as he studied each tassel, the incredibly detailed script was brilliantly beautiful. "What is that" the large man whispered, again taking a step closer to get a better look. Darius smiled flatly. "It is something only a Speaker can use, my friend," he stated and then, closing his eyes, breathing the words "Videre Verum corpus," pushing his will into the phrase as he felt the thin woven leather heat. A gasp escaped the large man's mouth as he once again wiped away the sweat on his shiny bald head. Murat's brown eyes were  alight  with wonder as he stared at the bracelet in fascination. As he watched, the runic letters on the tassels began to pulse a glowing green color. Darius seemed not to notice as his eyes remained closed, repeating the strange words over and over his face set in a determined mask. The more he repeated the words, the more the letters began to glow, no longer pulsing but instead staying a steady green, the glow increasing with every repetition of the phrase.   Darius moved his arm over the body as a green smoke began to emanate from the weaved leather band, falling over the body it began to cover the dead Prince. Murat motioned to take a step forward, and the Speakers other hand shot up to stop him. The gesture forceful enough to stop the makeshift mortician in his tracks. Repeating the words, Darius pushed more of his will into the magic as the smoke enveloped the entire corpse. Once it was covered, Darius pulled the arm away, his cloak covering the band as the green glow began to dissipate. As both men watched, the smoke rose from the body, forming a perfect simulacrum of the Prince above him. Leaning in, Darius studied the smoke. "Notice my friend, there are no entry wounds, no weapons used on the prince, whatever killed him was not physical," he began, and with a wave of his hand, the smoke replica rotated, giving him a full view of the body.   Suddenly Darius held his hand, and the simulacrum stopped a section of the replicant's smoky arm pulsed with white light. "What is this?" Darius whispered, expanding his fingers, and the smoke expanded, making the floating representation grow to double in size. "Look at this, my friend, it appears to be something burned into our dear prince's hand and arm," Darius whispered and motioned Murat forward. The large man shuffled slowly as if scared of the thing floating above the table. "What is it? What does it say?" he whispered,  looking between Darius and the floating visual. "It's a word, though I am not familiar with it," he said, though not to anyone in particular, and with a final wave of his hand, the smoky apparition disappeared. "drazahoib," Murat whispered as if the word itself were a weapon he was afraid would go off. "It is not a word I am familiar with, nor is it one that I have seen used by  Mage s, however, with what the investigators for the King have been studying. They seem to be leaning in that direction and that my friend could be very, very dangerous," Darius stated, staring off into space as he thought of the repercussions should they discover a  Mage  was behind the assassination of a monarch. "It appears I have my work cut out for me," he said, and with that, Darius turned and headed back for the door. Returning to his escort, he nodded at the old man. "Take me to where the prince spent most of his time," and the old man nodded, motioning for the Speaker to follow. A short time later, after a myriad of halls and stairwells, Darius found himself in the  castles  attic, an old dusty wooden chamber filled with ancient relics carefully laid upon shelves. Along the entire outer wall of the old room, in the center stood three tables circling a large firepit, the pit. However, blackened and well used stood silent and dark, candles, and lanterns dotted the entire room. The old man went around lighting them, and areas of the old chamber began to illuminate, highlighting the items and relics clearly, the likes of which the Speaker had never seen. Walking amongst the dusty tables and shelves, he picked up item after item, studying the ancient relics, coming to a strange looking weapon. Darius gently picked up a strange looking knife running the hilt. He appreciated the feel of the odd material, soft yet firm. The blade's base held more of the peculiar lettering, this one reading 'Ontario'; studying the black blade,  Darius moved it back and forth, allowing the light to catch the odd thin paint over the metal. He had never seen its equal, not even in the high-quality  Mage  weapons he had seen forged within the Order; putting the knife back, he looked along the other interesting relics, finally resolving himself to the task at hand. "Where are we?" Darius asked the old man, who had returned to the entrance, standing there silently awaiting the Speaker's next orders. "You asked me to take you to where the Prince spent most of his time. This was his passion, he collected relics of the ancient world, of the first ones, since the only ones that existed landed when man returned to earth, they were rare, most having been lost to the ages, the Prince split his time between digs or seeking out collectors like himself. This was where they found him, Speaker," the old man finished, pointing to the closest table "he was lying there, some of the relics had fallen around him, he had been dead only a short time, no one was found with him. However, there is suspicion over who might have done it," he finished and looked at Darius pointedly.  Mages , he thought to himself, turning his back to the old man, not wanting to show the anger that flashed across his face. Darius instead took to studying the tables, looking over the handwritten notebooks and the relics lined along display cases. Some he could guess at their use, and others were a complete mystery, he thought. Picking up another item, one side covered in a dark glass, and the other had lettering, he did not recognize it, sounding out the best he could "Samsung," he whispered and with a shrug, gently replaced the item on the display shelf. Darius could imagine this was a place of solace for the young Prince, for one who every moment was planned and analyzed, who was critiqued at every move and statement,  this was a place he could get away and be himself. "Who was in charge of his security that night? I will need to speak with him," Darius commanded, and the old man nodded, disappearing out the door, leaving the Speaker alone in the cavernous warehouse of relics. It didn't take long before the old man returned with a rather unpleasant looking squat soldier in the shiniest armor that Darius had ever seen. F rom the look of it, the man must spend hours polishing it , Darius thought as the old man moved to the side, allowing this squat hulking specimen of a man to pass. The guard marched over to Darius, and clicking his heels, stood at rigid attention before announcing himself. "Guard Captain Heathrow reporting, sir," the man barked, causing Darius to wince at the volume. "At ease soldier," he waived and, for a moment, watched as the Soldier bristled. " Its  captain, sir," he corrected, the Sir coming out less like a sign of respect and more like a slur, Darius mused. Darius stood there for what seemed like an eternity until finally, the cheers died down, and the square went silent. "You were never meant to succeed, Darius, you were simply a distraction, one I needed to ensure that the King would listen to my council," came a familiar voice from the stairs. Darius turned to find Margo leaning against the door frame. "What, what are you talking about?" he asked, her voice had changed. It sounded  ..  different somehow, almost jubilant, he thought as Margo stood upright and slowly approached him. "Poor Darius, so easily manipulated, the girl was always going to die, but since I was the one who desperately tried to save her life, I was the voice of reason, the voice of logic, when it came time to kill the girl. I gave the King the gentle push he needed, and since I had been the one against it, at least openly, he listened, as I knew he would," she almost purred as a malicious smile broke out across her face. "Prepare for War, my child, it will come and soon," she finished, passing Darius and continuing over to the open window, and as he watched, the Margo he had seen melted away. Changing before his eyes as the older woman became younger and  taller, the muted greying hair changed to bright blonde, and after a few moments, a beautiful and regal creature stood contemplating the sun". Darius stood there for a moment, trying to comprehend what he was seeing. "Who are you" he finally was able to say. The woman turned and smiled at him. "You can call me The Black Queen," she said as her body burst into a hundred ravens which poured out the window, leaving the Speaker alone as the pounding from the stage continued to reverberate throughout the room.
